proposal.competing_explanation: Reducing obstacle_height alters the instrumented-state observation vector (heightmap, contact normals, proximity sensors) fed to the 650-parameter waypoint MLP, shifting its predicted waypoints in a way that changes the approach trajectory but still results in protected contact through a different failure mode (e.g., earlier collision or different contact geometry).
proposal.hypothesis: Lowering obstacle_height from 0.17 to 0.065 reduces physical interference between the obstacle and protected geometry during payload approach and placement, decreasing protected_max_angle (currently 2.27 rad vs 0.05 threshold) and protected_max_displacement (0.132 vs 0.003 threshold) by providing more clearance for the gripper-payload system to maneuver without disturbing the protected object.

context.design: One changed initial-scene factor; exact same policy/task and paired nuisance draws. Height/friction change both scene physics and instrumented observations. No mid-episode restoration or final-test access.

friction.physics: Changes the shared default sliding-friction coefficient on scene geoms, including payload, fingers, table, tray and protected block; also changes the instrumented friction estimate.

obstacle_height.physics: Changes the protected block's height and center z=height/2. The obstacle IS the protected object; it is not a separate barrier or a heightmap.

payload_yaw.physics: Changes initial payload orientation around world z, in addition to the registered small yaw nuisance.

tray_offset_y.physics: Moves the target tray in world y; the fixed motion controller also uses the observed target location.

context.input_boundary: Exactly these eight scalar measurements enter the MLP once at reset. There are no heightmaps, contact-normal inputs, proximity sensors, images, or online contact feedback in this policy. Contacts are evaluator evidence, not policy observations.

mechanism_choices.clearance_contact: The commanded transfer path may lack clearance over the protected block, allowing finger or payload contact.
mechanism_choices.factor_interaction: The observed failure may depend on multiple scene factors, so changing one alone may leave the failure unresolved.
mechanism_choices.grasp_retention: Contact friction and the commanded finger closure may be insufficient to retain the payload.
mechanism_choices.lateral_alignment: Payload orientation or target displacement may bring the transport path into contact with the protected object.
mechanism_choices.learned_waypoint_response: Changing an instrumented policy input may change the learned lift and closure targets as well as the physical scene.
mechanism_choices.target_placement: The released payload may not lie within the registered target containment region.
